page.title: Pointers and memory
page.desc: A pointer is a variable holding an address. Pointer arithmetic, null, dangling pointers and buffer overruns are where C's power and its security record both come from.
page.intro: A pointer is a variable holding an address. Pointer arithmetic, null, dangling pointers and buffer overruns are where C's power and its security record both come from.

synapses.text: &x yields the address of x; *p reads or writes what p points at; p + 1 advances by one element, not one byte.
Use-after-free, double free, buffer overflow and null dereference are all pointer misuse; Rust's ownership model was designed to make them compile errors.
